thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: KCACHE-SVC p99 latency spike in us-west-2. Error rate on /v1/generate rose to 3.8% over the last 5m. Potential KV cache eviction storm + batching contention. Paging oncall: @sam. Incident ID INC-2026-1782

sam: I'm on it. grabbing metrics from grafana now and tailing kv logs.

will: fyi I see a config rollout 2m ago: `continuous_batching.optimizations=aggressive` (rev d3f7a). Not sure if it's related but it's suspicious.

sam: logs showing huge eviction pressure, lots of slices moved to paging. snippet:```
kv_evictions_total: 12432
kv_paged_reads: 9821
batch_waiters_short: 720
batch_waiters_long: 83
queue_length_short: 560
queue_length_long: 28
```

maria: that queue pattern looks like short requests starving. batch scheduler is prioritizing large kv-backed requests due to batching heuristics.

jen: I'm toggling back the continuous batching flag in canary to see. `PATCH /configs/continuous_batching { enabled: false }`

deploy-bot: Rollback job started for config `continuous_batching` (canary -> prod guard). job id rb-178234-3.

alex: temporarily applying ingress throttles to heavy streaming routes to give the scheduler breathing room: `rate-limit /models/*/stream 100rps` across us-west-2 for 10m.

support: Customer impact: AcmePay experiencing 15% increase in latency and 2 customers reported errors inside their flows. Not widespread but visible. Marking affected customers list in support tracker.

sam: setting incident severity to SEV2 (partial impact to a subset of customers). I'll own triage and initial doc.

will: after rollback started I'm seeing reduced batch_waiters_long but `queue_length_short` still high — looks like cache eviction caused working sets for short requests to be paged out. short requests now incur increased cold-starts into kv and are getting queued behind large requests.

jen: flipping `scheduler.fairness_mode=preemptive` in canary so short requests get prioritized immediately. Command:```
/cfg set scheduler.fairness_mode preemptive --env canary
```

jen: also bumping `short_request_weight=3` for the scheduler.

deploy-bot: scheduler fairness patch deployed to canary (patch id sf-1782). Monitoring metrics.

maria: adding temporary eviction limit to KV: `kv.max_evictions_per_minute=2000` to slow the eviction storm while we stabilize.

sam: oncall handoff in 30m to jen. I'll stay for the handoff and then hand ownership. Jen, you have the timeline and runbook.

jen: got it. I'll continue monitoring, coordinate with support for customer comms, and own postmortem. creating follow-up channel #incident-1782345678 now. please move ongoing chatter there.

alex: quick note — removed the aggressive quantization cache optimizer that was part of rev d3f7a (it was expanding per-request KV page usage). Reverted that PR.

support: AcmePay updated: errors decreased after throttle and rollback; they see degraded performance but no errors after 8m.

sam: preliminary hypothesis: a recent batching/optimizer change increased per-request KV working set and reduced locality. That caused a KV eviction surge which paged hot keys. The batch scheduler's prior heuristic then allowed long/large requests to accumulate and consume execution slots, starving short requests and causing p99 cliffs.

will: hotfix ready for scheduler: add short-request preemption + cap on batch size when kv_paging_rate > 5000/min. patch:```
if (kv_paging_rate > 5000) {
  scheduler.max_batch_size = min(scheduler.max_batch_size, 8);
  scheduler.enable_preemptive_short = true;
}
```

deploy-bot: hotfix deployed to prod at 1782349021 (hotfix id hot-178234-sched). Observability: p99 dropped ~55% in the first 3m post-deploy.

maria: creating action items: [1] revert optimizer permanently and audit similar flags, [2] increase KV capacity for hot keys, [3] add metrics/alert: `kv_paging_rate > 2000` triggers canary adjustments, [4] add scheduler unit test for mixed workloads. I'll own the follow-ups and postmortem.

support: sending initial customer advisory to AcmePay and impacted accounts. recommending app-level retries for short window.

sam: handing primary to jen (jen will run the incident). I'll remain available for 15m to assist with logs.

jen: thanks team. summary for postmortem: root cause = optimizer change increased per-request working set -> KV eviction storm -> increased paging -> batch scheduler starvation for short requests -> tail latency spike. Mitigations = rollback config, temporary throttles, scheduler fairness hotfix, KV eviction rate cap.

jen: postmortem owner: maria; timeline owner: sam; follow-up owner for scheduler tests: will. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.

sam: closing this thread and moving active updates to #incident-1782345678. Great rapid response, nice cross-team coordination :thumbsup:
